findings.body: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run` (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:127-157), the code attempts to catch `queue.ShutDown` exceptions, but the standard Python `queue` module does not define a `ShutDown` exception. This will cause an unhandled exception if such an exception is raised or the except clause will never be triggered, potentially causing the thread to hang or crash unexpectedly.
findings.suggestion: Remove the except clauses for `queue.ShutDown` or replace them with appropriate exception handling for queue operations, such as handling `queue.Empty` or using a sentinel value to signal shutdown.
findings.title: Catching nonexistent `queue.ShutDown` exception in OrderedQueueWorker.run

findings.body: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:231-244), the method calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` on each queue. However, Python's standard `queue.Queue` does not have a `shutdown` method, which will raise an AttributeError at runtime. This will prevent the worker threads from shutting down properly and may cause the consumer to hang or crash during shutdown.
findings.suggestion: Replace `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` with a sentinel value insertion or use a different mechanism to signal the queue to stop. For example, put a special sentinel object in each queue to unblock workers and allow them to exit.
findings.title: Calling nonexistent `shutdown` method on queue.Queue in FixedQueuePool.shutdown

models.summary: The change adds a new thread-queue-parallel processing mode with a fixed queue pool and worker threads. The implementation has critical bugs related to incorrect use of Python's queue.Queue: calling a nonexistent `shutdown` method and catching a nonexistent `queue.ShutDown` exception. These issues will cause runtime errors and prevent proper shutdown of worker threads.
